model_annotation: The bar chart displays the effect sizes of various linguistic features across different language families, with the x-axis representing language families (including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic) and the y-axis representing the effect size, ranging from 0 to 30. Each bar is color-coded and corresponds to a specific linguistic feature, with a legend indicating the following: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light red), and XLM-B2 (dark red). The chart shows that for most language families, the effect sizes vary significantly between the different linguistic features, with XLM-B2 and mBERT-B2 generally showing higher effect sizes compared to other features. The effect sizes for the IE-Slavic family are particularly high, with XLM-B2 reaching above 20, while the Isolate category shows very low effect sizes across all features. Error bars are present for each bar, indicating variability or uncertainty in the measurements. The bars are grouped by language family, with each group containing six bars corresponding to the six linguistic features. The chart is rotated, with the x-axis labels oriented diagonally.
